title: Enterprise offer readiness + copy variants (wip)
body:
Purpose

This is a working playbook for enterprise-grade marketplace offers (AWS/Azure/GCP + private/managed offers). The doc bundles: acceptance checklists, SKU/entitlement scaffolding, short/long copy variants tuned for security-conscious buyers, and a go/no-go QA matrix. Intended audience: GTM PMs, partner success, legal pre-sales, and engineering onboarding owners.

Status and notes
- WIP: copy variants below are draft-first-pass. Need legal review for export control phrasing and trademark calls.
- Priority: prioritize AWS & Azure private offers first due to two active partner deals (see JIRA-GTM-4821).
- TODO: confirm trial SKU mapping with Billing (Mei), and include marketplace-specific screenshots.

High-level acceptance checklist (must be green before publish)
- Product metadata: long and short descriptions provided (see copy).
- Offer type selected: SaaS / AMI / Private Offer / Dedicated Capacity + mapping documented.
- Entitlements & SKUs: 1 trial SKU + 2 paid SKUs (monthly, annual) defined and verified with finance.
- Metering/billing tests: 3 end-to-end test invoices in sandbox for each marketplace.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 summary uploaded, data processing addendum (DPA) available, KMS options documented.
- Networking: VPC peering/Private Link or private endpoint instructions ready for private deployments.
- Support model: published SLA table + contact process for escalation.
- Legal: marketplace contract clauses reviewed; export controls & sanctions checklist applied.
- Marketing assets: logo at required sizes, 1 hero screenshot, 3 feature screenshots, short demo video link.

Technical preflight (engineering checklist)
- API endpoints: production and sandbox URLs listed and tested.
- Authentication: token/OAuth flows documented; sample SDK snippet for 3 languages.
- Deployment manifest: container image + version, GPU requirements (per model), region availability matrix.
- Observability hooks: recommended CloudWatch/Stackdriver traces and Redwood Console integration documented.
- Rollback plan: documented fallback to smaller model variant and region reroute for capacity failures.

SKUs & entitlement sketch (example)
- SKU-TRIAL-30D: 30-day trial, limited throughput (2 rps), no committed billing, auto-expire.
- SKU-LITE-M: monthly, metered per-token, burst-cap allowed up to 5 rps.
- SKU-PRO-ANNUAL: annual commit, discounted unit price, reserved GPU capacity option.
Notes: map internal product tiers to marketplace SKUs; include feature gating flags (KV-caching, dedicated KV-store).

Copy variants (do not copy verbatim into marketplace - edit per vendor rules)
1) Short tagline (6–10 words)
- "High-throughput LLM inference for production apps"
- "Predictable latency. Lower inference costs."

2) 150-char elevator (for listing card)
- "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—built for production reliability and controlled costs."

3) 500-char overview (detailed listing blurb)
- "Redwood Inference is a production-first inference platform that ensures consistent latency, cost control, and operational visibility for LLM-powered features. Ship quickly with a hosted API, scale with reserved dedicated pools, or run privately in your VPC for regulated workloads. Features include automatic batching and prefix caching, model versioning and safe rollouts, per-route billing, and built-in fallbacks to maintain availability during load or region outages."

4) Feature bullets (short)
- "Fast, GPU-optimized serving runtime with continuous batching"
- "Automatic prefix and KV cache to reduce token cost"
- "Canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automated fallback policies"
- "Dedicated deployments: SLA-backed capacity and isolation"
- "Private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs"

5) Enterprise-focused benefit statements (for legal/compliance-minded buyers)
- "Data residency and private control plane options for regulated industries"
- "Audit-ready logging and key management integrations (bring-your-own KMS supported)"
- "Detailed cost breakdown: token-level and route-level analytics for chargebacks"

6) CTA variations
- Primary: "Start a 30-day trial"
- Secondary: "Request a private deployment evaluation"
- Technical CTA: "View API quickstart and SDK examples"

Marketplace-specific notes (quick vendor callouts)
- AWS: include AMI listing if we provide AMI-based private deploy. Ensure AWS Marketplace product qualified software vendor (PPSV) checklist entries complete. Private Offers: confirm AWS invoice flow for reserved capacity.
- Azure: map SKUs to Azure Marketplace meter dimensions and validate Azure entitlements API for seat vs consumption billing model. Note: Azure requires logo in SVG plus 1024x1024 PNG.
- GCP: single-tenant solutions should be published as Private Catalog entries; verify Cloud Billing export configuration.

QA acceptance matrix (quick)
- Metadata completeness: short + long copy, tags present, categories assigned -> owner: Priya -> pass/fail
- Billing test: sandbox invoice created for monthly and annual SKUs -> owner: Mei -> pass/fail
- Security docs: SOC2 + DPA uploaded -> owner: Diego -> pass/fail
- Integration test: SDK snippet runs sample generate request in sandbox -> owner: Eng-oncall -> pass/fail

Compliance & legal highlights (notes to legal)
- Export control: confirm language for cryptographic export and model usage in sanctioned regions.
- Privacy: in-line DPA summary for listing (short bullet) + link to full DPA.
- Audit: recommend including a one-page SOC2 TL;DR on listing page for enterprise browsing.

Operational runbook snippets (for post-publish)
- Incident: if model variant fails, marketplace listing should link to status page and recommended mitigation steps for customers (fallback to hosted API region).
- Billing dispute: map marketplaces' dispute contact to Redwood billing ops and provide template email for partners.

Localization & accessibility checklist
- Short + long copy localized for en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP.
- Accessibility: alt text for all screenshots, transcripts for demo video.

Marketing assets & examples (deliverables list)
- One-line summary, 150-char blurb, 500-char overview (all above).
- 3 feature screenshots + hero image (PNG/SVG).
- 60-90s demo video, transcript, and SRT captions.
- Logo pack (SVG, PNG 1024px) and product icon.

Open questions / decisions
- Are we enabling free-tier indefinite for open-source evaluation customers? Impact: entitlements and abuse detection.
- How do we label quantization/accuracy tradeoffs in listing copy without causing product confusion?
- Should we create separate listings for hosted API vs Dedicated/Private or combine under single offer with add-on SKUs?

Next steps (owner actions)
- Mei: confirm SKU price points and billing test plan (due 2026-03-17).
- Diego: upload SOC2 summary + DPA link and confirm legal-approved copy (due 2026-03-14).
- Engineering: provide sandbox API endpoints and SDK snippets (PR #77).
- Priya (GTM): finalize marketplace tag taxonomy and schedule listing publication window.

Notes to future reviewers
- This doc is intentionally product-focused and assumes marketplaces will allow us to surface technical details. If marketplace policy restricts wording (some don't allow pricing in listing body), update the copy accordingly.

Patch history
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-01-12: added SKU sketch and trial flow (Mei)
- 2026-03-10: updated compliance notes and QA matrix (Priya)

-----
End of working doc.

(Internal: do not publish this JSON blob directly to marketplace. Extract copy and assets into vendor-specific submission templates.)
